name: Source and screen direct private equity opportunities
summary: Private Equity deal teams in North America, Europe and Asia receive sale processes from banks and invitations from partner funds to co-control or minority stakes, and decide quickly whether each one is worth the team's time. Most are declined from the teaser or the information memorandum; the rest go to a weekly pipeline meeting, a management meeting, limited diligence and a non-binding first-round indication. Only about a quarter of opportunities reach deep diligence. Waiting on NDAs, management presentations, weekly meetings and the seller's round-one decision makes up most of the elapsed time, and much analysis is spent on deals that are later lost or declined.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager whose 166-person Private Equity department invests directly alongside partner funds and through fund commitments and secondaries.
baseline.notes: Fund commitments, secondaries and passive GP co-investments have their own processes and are excluded.

trigger: A banker's teaser or a partner's invitation to a direct private equity deal reaches a deal team.
end_state: The group head accepts a screening memo and the deal enters deep diligence, or the opportunity is declined or lost.

volume.seasonality: Fewer processes in spring 2020 during the pandemic and many in the second half of calendar 2021.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate derived from closings and the survey funnel; likely high for direct private equity alone (see assumptions).

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Virtual data rooms run by sellers and advisors
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Compliance system for personal trading, attestations and restricted lists

steps.name: Log the opportunity in the deal pipeline
steps.description: An analyst records an incoming opportunity (a banker's teaser for a sale process or a call from a partner fund offering a co-control or minority stake) in the deal pipeline with company, sector, region, size, seller, adviser and deadline, and assigns it to the coverage team.

evidence.note: Opportunities arrive as banker teasers or partner invitations (Macabacus; DPE invests alongside partners, F2021). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: First look at the teaser against the mandate
steps.description: An associate reads the teaser or partner note, checks size, sector, geography, ownership structure, partner quality and expected equity cheque against the program mandate and current pipeline, and writes a few lines on fit for the principal.

error.defect_description: Good fit dismissed or poor fit passed on.

evidence.note: Fit with the fund is one of the selection factors in the survey (GKM); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether to sign the NDA
steps.description: The principal reads the first-look note and decides whether to sign the non-disclosure agreement and request the information memorandum, or to decline and tell the banker or partner.

control.basis: Program mandate and deployment guidance set through capital allocation

evidence.note: Share declined before partner review is set so that 61.8 of 100 opportunities reach a partner group review, as in the survey funnel.

steps.name: Review and negotiate the NDA
steps.description: In-house counsel reviews the seller's non-disclosure agreement for scope, term, non-solicitation, standstill and residuals clauses and the fund's standard positions, marks it up and agrees the final text with the seller's counsel.

control.basis: Legal sign-off on confidentiality agreements under the fund's contracting authority

evidence.note: Buyers sign a confidentiality agreement before receiving the memorandum (Macabacus); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the executed NDA and information memorandum
steps.description: The seller's counsel and banker countersign the NDA and release the information memorandum and any initial data. A few processes are pulled or the fund is not given access.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the NDA and target in the compliance system
steps.description: The associate records the signed NDA, target and counterparties in the compliance system so Compliance can see the confidential relationship and, for a listed target, add it to the watch list.

error.defect_description: NDA not recorded; watch list incomplete.

control.basis: Insider trading law and the fund's information barrier policy for confidential information on listed targets

evidence.note: Formal conflicts clearance happens at the start of pim-pe-direct-due-diligence; this record is the author's estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Review the information memorandum and build a quick returns screen
steps.description: The associate reads the information memorandum, spreads the historical financials, and builds a simple buyout or co-investment returns model with entry multiple, leverage, growth and exit cases to see whether target returns are achievable at the likely price.

evidence.note: Bidders work from the 50+ page memorandum (Macabacus); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pull comparable deals and industry data
steps.description: An analyst pulls trading comparables, precedent transactions, industry growth data and any previous fund work on the sector or company, and adds them to the model and memo appendix.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether to take it to the pipeline meeting
steps.description: The principal reviews the quick returns screen and comparables and decides whether the opportunity is worth group discussion or should be declined now.

evidence.note: Combined with s03, sets 61.8% of opportunities reaching a partner group review (GKM funnel).

steps.name: Write the screening memo
steps.description: A senior associate writes a short screening memo: business and market, investment thesis, partner and governance, valuation and returns range, key risks, ESG flags, fit with the mandate and the resources needed to pursue it.

evidence.note: Memo topics follow the survey's selection factors (business model, management, ability to add value, valuation); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Group pipeline meeting reviews the opportunity
steps.description: At the weekly pipeline meeting the group head and team discuss the memo against other live opportunities and decide to pursue it with management meetings and limited diligence, ask for more information, or decline.

control.basis: Group-level review of opportunities before resources are committed

evidence.note: Shares set so that 52.8 of 100 opportunities meet management (GKM funnel). Only the group head's time is counted.

steps.name: Meet management or the partner
steps.description: The principal and senior associate attend the management presentation or a call with the partner fund, test the business plan, management quality and the partner's thesis and governance proposals, and write up notes.

evidence.note: 52.8% of considered opportunities reach a management meeting (GKM). Scheduling waits are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run limited due diligence
steps.description: The senior associate refines the model with management's plan, calls a few industry experts, reviews key customer, margin and leverage questions, and lists issues that would need deep diligence.

error.defect_description: Critical issue not found until deep diligence.

next.condition: potentially material ESG or climate exposure

evidence.note: 49.1% of considered opportunities get limited due diligence (GKM), so about 7% of those meeting management drop here. Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Screen for material ESG and climate risks
steps.description: A Sustainable Investing specialist checks the sector against the materiality framework, looks for controversies, and where climate risk may be material applies a first pass of the climate security selection framework, then sends red flags to the team.

control.basis: Climate Change Security Selection Framework applied at the screening stage where climate risk may be material

evidence.note: Framework applied during screening and due diligence (2022 report); share and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the first-round indication
steps.description: The senior associate drafts the non-binding indication of interest or partner term outline: valuation range, structure and equity cheque, key assumptions, conditions, financing approach and timetable for confirmatory work.

evidence.note: Preliminary non-binding bids end round 1 (Macabacus, Wall Street Prep); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the bid range and letter
steps.description: A director checks the valuation range against the model, comparables and the group's return targets, edits the letter's conditions and sends it back or forwards it for approval.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Group head approves the indication
steps.description: The group head approves submitting the non-binding indication within the group's authority, refers a very large indication to the department head, or decides not to bid.

control.basis: PE delegated authorities for non-binding bids under the fund's governing act s.35 investment policies

next.condition: very large indication, refer to department head

evidence.note: Investment policies and procedures required by the Act; PE bid authorities are not public and shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Department head approves a very large indication
steps.description: The Global Head of Private Equity reviews the largest indications for fit with deployment plans and concentration, and approves or stops them.

control.basis: PE delegated authorities for large commitments under the fund's governing act s.35 investment policies

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit the indication
steps.description: The associate sends the signed indication letter to the banker or partner by the deadline and updates the pipeline record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the seller's round-two decision
steps.description: The banker and seller compare indications and decide which bidders to invite to the second round; a partner decides whether to bring the fund in. Some sellers ask bidders to improve their range first.

next.condition: invited to the second round or partner confirms

evidence.note: Round 1 runs 4-6 weeks and indications narrow the buyer list (Wall Street Prep); invitation share is set so that 23.7% of opportunities reach deep diligence (GKM).

steps.name: Update the screening memo with the diligence plan
steps.description: The senior associate updates the screening memo with the round-one outcome, the price range, the main diligence questions, the advisers needed and their budget, and the timetable.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Group head accepts the screening memo
steps.description: The group head approves entering deep diligence with the adviser budget and staffing, which hands the deal to the due diligence team, or stops it if priorities have changed.

control.basis: Group head approval to commit adviser spending and staff to deep diligence

evidence.note: This matches the trigger of pim-pe-direct-due-diligence; share is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Declined at first look
exceptions.description: The teaser shows the deal is outside the mandate on size, sector, region or structure.

exceptions.name: Declined after the information memorandum
exceptions.description: The quick returns screen shows the likely price cannot reach target returns.

exceptions.name: Declined at the pipeline meeting
exceptions.description: The group prefers other opportunities or sees a key risk.

exceptions.name: Not selected for round two
exceptions.description: The seller picks higher or more certain bidders after first-round indications.

exceptions.name: Asked to improve the indication
exceptions.description: The banker asks bidders to raise their range before choosing round-two bidders.

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)

sources.title: 2022 Report on Sustainable Investing
sources.supports: Climate Change Security Selection Framework applied during the screening and due diligence stages of deals where climate risk is potentially material; structured reviews of material sustainability factors for potential direct private equity investments

sources.title: What Do Private Equity Firms Say They Do? (NBER Working Paper 21133)
sources.publisher: National Bureau of Economic Research (Gompers, Kaplan and Mukharlyamov)
sources.supports: Deal funnel per 100 opportunities considered: 61.8 reviewed with partner group or investment committee, 52.8 meet management, 49.1 limited due diligence, 23.7 deep due diligence, 22.5 offer terms, 13.6 sign LOI, 6.1 close; closed deals 35.6% proactively self-generated and 33.3% investment-bank generated; business model and competitive position is the top selection factor, then management, ability to add value and valuation

sources.title: Sale Process Types: Auctions & Negotiated Sales
sources.supports: Buyers receive a 1-5 page teaser, sign a confidentiality agreement, receive a 50+ page information memorandum and submit preliminary non-binding bids, after which selected bidders are invited to further due diligence; broad auctions have more than ten bidders, targeted auctions three to ten, negotiated sales one or two; auctions take four to five months to a signed agreement

sources.title: Sell Side M&A: Auction Process and Timeline Example
sources.supports: Round 1 of an auction runs 4-6 weeks with NDAs, the CIM and non-binding indications of interest used to narrow the buyer list; Round 2 runs 4-6 weeks with management meetings, data room diligence and final bids; negotiations 6-8 weeks

sources.title: Unveiling a decade of M&A diligence trends: key insights for deal success
sources.supports: Average time from data room opening to announcement rose to 203 days; private targets average about 230 days before announcement versus 125 for public targets; cross-border deals add about 30 days

sources.title: the fund's governing act (S.C. 1997, c. 40), sections 34 and 35
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
sources.supports: The board must establish investment policies, standards and procedures that a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in dealing with the property of others, and the Board must follow them

assumptions: Branch shares follow the Gompers, Kaplan and Mukharlyamov funnel (61.8% partner review, 52.8% management meeting, 49.1% limited diligence, 23.7% deep diligence), so about 28 of 120 monthly opportunities feed the 28 cases a month of pim-pe-direct-due-diligence.

The process map volume of 120 opportunities a month looks high for direct private equity alone; the DPE portfolio grew from 85 to 88 investments in fiscal 2021. It may include Asia direct deals and partner co-investments, or the survey funnel may be tighter at this fund.
The last step (group head accepts the screening memo) is the trigger of pim-pe-direct-due-diligence, which then runs conflicts clearance, adviser engagement and round-two work.
Partner-sourced deals (35% of cases) are modelled on the same path as banker-led auctions; for them the round-two decision is the partner's choice to bring the fund in.
The pipeline meeting and approval steps count only the decision maker's time although others attend.

legal_counsel and si_specialist are organisation roles not listed for this process; they are added for NDA review and ESG screening. Other PE time is within the headcount the organisation file gives each role after existing claims.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file and include large incentive pay.
